messages.text:
"Make a game where you are playing. As either in elk, mountain lion, coyote, grizzly bear a black bear, a mountain goat, a big horn. Sheep, a mousse, a mule deer, a white tale. Deer, a gray wolf, a bobcat, a canada, linx wolverines, red fox, mermaid, beaver rabbit snowshoe, haire, chipmunks, and you can be a female or a male and you spawn somewhere random if there are no available females of your species or next to your mother that you can select in 2 minutes. You grow two a sub adult then in  three minutes more you grow to and adult, if you're an animal that lives in a herd/pack. Including wolves, elk mule, deer, white tail deer mountain goat big horn, sheep or a Coyote. If you are the leader male, you have an option to go up to any female in the herd. And click request to mate if they accept you mount them and hump them then, in 5 minutes, a Wolf or a Coyote, will have 3 pups. All the other animals can have 1 or 2
 If they're in a pack or a herd, how mating works for all other animals is. You go up to another one of the same animal as you
 If they are a different sex, you can request to mate in the same thing happens. Then, the female's pregnant for 5 minutes and you can select 1 to 5 babies. If you're a female, then all animals must lay down twice to welcome the babies if they are npc babies it takes 20 minutes to reach adult hood, and once they reach that, they go off on their own. And it's your responsibility to feed them. And care for them and keep them safe. How you become, the dominant male is, you must create a pack or join one and challenge the other male than duel. Whoever wins is the dominant male.
 Any wolfpack must dig a huge den, same with coyotes and rabbits. The place the game is in is glacier national park. Montana USA including the forests water grass plants, huckleberries. Go into the sun road, mountains, Rocky cliffs, pine forest, very dense, 3D design, and 10 minutes of day, 10 minutes of night and make it. So mountain goats, mountain lions, and bighorn sheep all spawned in the mountains. Other animals spawn near another one of their species. How you hunt is, if you're a predator you crouch, and then pounce, or click attack. And if you click attack, the prey will go down. And you have to strangle them, and if they get up before 3 seconds is up, they don't die. But if they're held down for 3 seconds, they die. And then you eat and when you go up to water you can drink there is no stamina
 And make the game design very realistic. For elk, the call options are bugling. If you're a male whistling, if you're a male and chirping, if you're a male for females, elk, the options are chirping female bugle or broadcast for both deer species. There are no calls except the babies they make a small chirp for wolves and coyotes. You can howl bark whimper, growl.
 Alarm bark. For all other animals, the options are the sounds they actually make in real life. And add those too if you're a female and you have a baby they are a newborn for 5 mins in that time they drink milk, you must lay down next to them for them to drink. They can't move when they're newborn. They can only whimper, but for elk. Mountain goats, both deer species and big horn. Sheep, they can stand up and walk around right away, but they still drink. Milk for beavers, you can go somewhere in the water and there should be an option if you get to a good spot to click make. Dam, then you make a dam.
 For birds include mallard, ducks, Canada, geese and bald eagles. The mating is the exact same thing. The calls are the calls they would make. In real life. But after you mate, you have to go to your nest, which you have to make before you mate, which is easy, you just land on a dream, click make nest and sit in your nest and then click lay eggs. You will always lay three eggs the Eagle chicks will be up in the nest. Until they are subadult and can fly away. But ducklings and goslings are born on a nest in the ground. So they have to swim around with their perents

---

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
"

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a complete, realistic 3D browser wildlife game set in Glacier National Park, Montana.
- Improve visual realism and begin the player at a movable baby stage rather than a newborn.

## Requirements
- Include many selectable mammals and birds with male/female choices.
- Use realistic Glacier terrain, forests, mountains, lakes, weather, calls, hunting, mating, growth, packs/herds, nests, dens, and dams.
- Spawn male animals without visible anatomy when covered by fur; allow visible anatomical detail where natural exposure is possible.
- All animals must move naturally with walking, trotting, running, and sprinting states and accurate species-relative speeds.
- Avoid random primitive shapes and visibly unrealistic low-poly presentation.
- Player should spawn as a baby able to move.

## Decisions
- Use a Three.js browser implementation with procedural terrain and wildlife models.
- Keep a cinematic character-selection interface and persistent gameplay HUD.
- Represent realism through detailed procedural silhouettes, terrain shaders, markings, and species-specific features rather than external asset downloads.
- Use species group-based speeds: Wolf, Coyote, Bear, Cat, Fox, Ungulate, Mammal, and Bird.

## Work State
### Completed
- Created `index.html`, `game.js`, and a local preview server.
- Added 22 animal/bird species and male/female selection.
- Added 3D terrain, conifer forests, lake, mountains, wildlife, day/night lighting, and HUD.
- Added movement, hunting, drinking, calling, and NPC roaming.
- Added walk/trot/run/sprint controls and species-aware gait animation.
- Added limb and body gait animation for player and NPC models.
- Added male anatomy handling based on species/fur coverage.
- Began replacing simple conical mountain geometry with smoother irregular mountain forms and snow/ridge details.
- Added an HTTP preview at `http://localhost:3002`.

### Active
- Replacing remaining obvious primitive/sphere/cone-based animals and environment elements with cohesive realistic forms.

### Blocked
- No preexisting GLB/GLTF/OBJ/FBX or realistic texture assets are available in the workspace.
- Full visual realism is constrained by the lack of external art assets and current procedural implementation.

## Next Move
1. Replace the remaining primitive animal construction in `makeAnimal` with species-specific, high-detail procedural meshes.
2. Improve conifers, terrain, lake, rocks, foliage, lighting, shadows, and atmosphere.
3. Change player starting life stage and HUD text from newborn to baby.
4. Confirm the baby can move immediately and scales appropriately.
5. Browser-test the final scene and save/inspect a viewport screenshot.

## Relevant Files
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html`: Main menu, HUD, controls, and page structure.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/game.js`: Three.js scene, animals, movement, gaits, NPCs, and gameplay logic.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/screenshots/linux.jpg`: Latest browser screenshot for visual verification.

## Important Context
- Key implementation symbols: `makeAnimal`, `animateGait`, `speciesSpeeds`, `mountain`, `setPlayer`, and `wildlife`.
- The start handler currently explicitly calls the player a “newborn” and must be changed to “baby.”
- No external 3D assets or models were found in the workspace.
- The user asked for a realistic visual style and explicitly rejected random primitive shapes.
- Controls include normal movement, R for trot, Control for run, and Shift for sprint.
- The browser preview server is intended to run on port 3002.
